body:
You are drafting dialogue for a dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd (D&D 5e; the valley of Barovia, ruled by the vampire Strahd). Reply in plain text only, no JSON, no markdown headings, and do not send messages to anyone else. Finish after one reply.

Setting: the Vistani camp at Tser Pool on the Old Svalich Road (wagons, a plank stage, horse pens, a fire). Four side quests here can now FAIL. A failure is a quiet story outcome, not a punishment: it should leave one specific image of what was lost and change what the player sees later. Never lecture, never blame the player more than once, no game terms. Lines are 1 to 2 sentences each (at most about 30 words). Speakers use the format `Name: text` (Narrator for narration, second person present tense: "You...", "The..."). Journal entries are in the party's own voice ("we"), past tense, one or two sentences, at most 40 words. A "journal warning" is one short in-fiction line (at most 14 words) shown while time is running out. Do not invent new named people or places.

QUEST A: Called by Name. Big Tobar's son Nelu walked off after his dead mother's voice; will-o'-wisps in the gorge under Tser Falls speak in the voices of the dead. Nelu is alive on a ledge in the gorge, three days hungry. If the party doesn't go to the falls after dark and bring him up within three days of Tobar asking, he answers the voices and goes over.
Existing Tobar lines: "Nobody here will go to the falls at night. I'm not asking anybody here. I'm asking you." / "Whatever calls you, don't answer it. Whoever it sounds like. Especially then. I said that to strangers on the road for twenty years, and I never once thought to say it to my own son."
A1. Tobar, one more line when the party agrees, naming the time: three days already without food; he won't last three more.
A2. Journal entry when it fails (Nelu answered).
A3. Journal warning while the clock runs.
A4. Tobar afterwards at the camp fire, two lines: grief, specific to a wheelwright (he mends wagon wheels).
A5. The falls after dark afterwards, two Narrator lines: the lights in the gorge are calling as before, and one of the voices is now Nelu's, calling "Da".

QUEST B: The Dancing Bear. Lavinia's dancing bear Bujor broke his chain and went up the deer path to a clearing at an old den, where a cub is caught in a hunter's iron trap; blights (moving knots of twigs, needles and vines) come toward anything that cries. The party can back away from the clearing; if they don't come back by the next day, Bujor fights the blights alone and dies, and the blights take the cub.
B1. One Narrator line as the party backs away from the clearing: the warning (the things in the trees are already moving toward the crying).
B2. Journal entry when it fails.
B3. Journal warning while it runs.
B4. The clearing afterwards, three Narrator lines: Bujor dead in the bruised fern, the broken chain, the trap open and empty, no cub.
B5. Lavinia afterwards on the plank stage, two lines once she knows (she found out from the trees, from the silence, or from the party's faces; keep it simple). Her existing voice: "Clap or don't, the steps are the same." / "He was always a better dancer than me. He knew when the dance was over."

QUEST C: The Grey Mare. Radu sold his grey mare Steaua to the black carriage; the castle turned her into a black horse with coals for eyes, and the party had to put her down. Radu pays the castle's gold over, but he used to also hand over an old "bride price" a trader once paid for the mare (a rod that turns curses back). Now, when she is lost, he keeps it.
C1. Radu, one or two lines: he keeps the bride price, it was hers, it stays on the gate with the black ribbon. Radu's voice: sly horse-trader with a soft heart ("I have a cure for that", "That's the first fair thing to happen in this camp all week").

QUEST D: The Hanged Man at the Crossroads. Luminita tends the camp's horses and waits for her brother Nicu, who rode to Vallaki to sell a mare; he hangs from the gallows at the crossroads with a HORSE THIEF board, because she told him to sell a mare she found. The party has seen the gallows. They can now lie to her.
D1. The party's option text (a short stage direction in parentheses, under 12 words): telling her they passed no one on the road.
D2. After the lie, one Narrator line: she goes back to brushing, and her eyes go to the road (the warning in hindsight: she will watch it every night).
D3. Journal entry (we let her keep waiting).
D4. Luminita on later visits, two lines: still no rider on the road, she has started sleeping in the wagon nearest the road. Her voice: sharp, proud, funny under grief ("He doesn't like strangers. Neither do I. It's nothing personal; we just have taste.").

Format your reply exactly as:
A1: Big Tobar: ...
A2: ...
(and so on through D4)
result:
A1: Big Tobar: He's been three days on that wet stone without a crust of bread. Give it three more, and the cold or his mother's voice will finish what the hunger started.
A2: We left Tser Falls to the dark for too long. By the time we looked into the gorge, Nelu had already answered the voices below.
A3: Nelu is starving on the gorge ledge; the voices call every night.
A4: Big Tobar: He used to hold the iron tire while I drove the spokes home, steady as an oak. Now I set two wedges where his hands ought to be, and the wheel still wobbles.
Big Tobar: A man can mend a split rim or a cracked axle before the kettle boils. There isn't a tool in my chest for this.
A5: Narrator: Pale lights drift through the mist beneath the falls, murmuring in stolen voices that echo off the wet rock.
Narrator: A new lantern-glow hangs lower than the rest, calling out for its Da in a thin, shivering boy's voice.
B1: Narrator: As you step back down the deer path, the wet needles rustle and knotted shapes in the underbrush begin creeping toward the cub's high, thin crying.
B2: We left Bujor in the clearing with the trapped cub and the creeping brush. When the woods went quiet, neither bear came down the path.
B3: The things in the trees are closing in on Bujor before dawn.
B4: Narrator: Bujor lies still in the crushed, blackened fern, snapped thorns tangled deep in his heavy coat.
Narrator: His broken iron chain trails into the mud beside him, cold and slick with rain.
Narrator: Beyond his outstretched paw, the hunter's iron jaws lie pried open and empty, with only a tuft of dark fur caught on the teeth.
B5: Lavinia: You don't have to say it; the woods up the hill have been quiet since daybreak, and I know what silence sounds like.
Lavinia: I took his brass collar off the post by the steps this morning. Tonight I dance alone, and the boards can creak for the both of us.
C1: Radu: The castle's gold is yours, every dirty coin of it, as promised. The old rod stays tied to the gatepost with her black ribbon—it was Steaua's bride price, and I'm not trading away the last thing that belonged to her.
D1: (Tell her you passed no one on the road from the crossroads.)
D2: Narrator: She goes back to drawing the stiff brush down the roan's flank, though her eyes lift toward the empty bend in the Old Svalich Road as the dusk settles.
D3: We told Luminita the road behind us was empty and kept the gallows at the crossroads to ourselves. She is still waiting for Nicu to ride back from Vallaki.
D4: Luminita: Still no sign of him on the road, which only means he's haggling some poor Vallaki stablemaster down to his boots.
Luminita: I moved my bedroll into the front wagon by the ditch—not for him, mind you, just so I can be the first to tell him how late he is.
